title: Python Errors and Debugging
description: Identify common Python errors and use the final traceback line to choose the next debugging step.

questions.prompt: What kind of error is a missing colon after an if statement?
questions.explanation: Python cannot parse the statement, so it reports a syntax error before running the program.

options: A name was used before it was defined or was misspelled
A list index was too large
A value was used with an incompatible operation
A requested module could not be imported
questions.correct: A name was used before it was defined or was misspelled
questions.explanation: Check spelling, scope, and whether the assignment statement ran before the name was used.

questions.prompt: The last line of a traceback often names the exception and gives the most useful first clue.
questions.explanation: The traceback path is useful too, but the final exception line usually identifies the immediate problem.

questions.prompt: What exception does this code raise?
questions.explanation: Division by zero is not defined for this operation, so Python raises ZeroDivisionError.

questions.prompt: What exception is likely from values = [1, 2]; values[2]?
questions.explanation: The valid indexes are 0 and 1; index 2 is outside the list.
The dictionary does not contain key b. get can provide a fallback when that behavior is appropriate.

questions.prompt: Changing a protected test file is a valid way to make an assignment pass.
questions.explanation: Tests describe the assignment contract. Changing them hides the problem and Ducky detects test tampering.

questions.prompt: What is a good first response to a failing assertion?
options: Compare the expected and actual values
Inspect only the last line of the test
Change the expected value until the test passes
Skip the failing assertion and continue
questions.correct: Compare the expected and actual values
questions.explanation: The difference tells you whether the issue is a value, type, branch, or formatting mistake.

questions.prompt: What exception does this code raise?
questions.explanation: The text cannot be parsed as an integer, so int raises ValueError.

questions.prompt: Why should you fix the first error before chasing later errors?
options: Later errors may be consequences of the first failure
The first error is always a style warning
questions.correct: Later errors may be consequences of the first failure
questions.explanation: One missing name or malformed statement can cause many downstream failures; fix the earliest clear cause first.
